key_findings: **candidate FUN_00D082A0 IS NOT THE SCHEDULE ENTRY POINT**. FindAllReferencesToAddress confirmed only 2 DATA refs, BOTH inside FUN_00CD8990 (the LGE bootstrap; see docs/client-architecture.md, 'The LGE class system is a 5-userdata-type model'). DATA refs = function-pointer registration as a cclosure. FUN_00D082A0 (264 bytes) is a TIME-GETTER exposed to Lua scripts - it reads the scheduler epoch, computes a time delta via FUN_004CFA50 (QueryPerformanceCounter wrapper) divided by DAT_00F909C8 (frequency), and returns a double seconds-since-epoch value. Likely registered as `_lge_getTime` or similar Lua API.

**MS-scheduler ENQUEUE PATH FULLY MAPPED**. Core enqueue function: [[LuaSchedulerMs_enqueue_core_FUN_00CEEE70]] (BCS-Y-1725 NEW, 500 bytes). Has 3 distinct callers: (1) [[LuaSchedulerTickMs_FUN_00CEF510]] (BCS-Y-1696) for re-enqueueing during tick scan; (2) [[LuaSchedulerMs_enqueue_schedule_if_not_pending_FUN_00CEF0F0]] (BCS-Y-1726 NEW, 1047 bytes) - the 'schedule(callback, delay) if not already pending' API with timeGetTime + dedup search; (3) [[LuaSchedulerMs_enqueue_batch_FUN_00CEF900]] (BCS-Y-1727 NEW, 184 bytes) - batch schedule over a vector<ushort> of event IDs. Both enqueue APIs eventually delegate to FUN_00CEEE70 for the actual R-B tree insertion.

**SCHEDULER QUEUES ARE RED-BLACK TREES, NOT LISTS** (refinement of the 'us-queue/ms-list' approximation). Evidence: (a) head nodes are sentinel pattern with 3-pointer initialization (left/right/parent self-refs), (b) color byte at fixed offset (+0x29 for us-tree node, +0x21 for ms-tree node) set to 1 (red) on init, (c) tick traversal in FUN_00CF6080 (us tick body, 856 bytes) walks tree via `cVar4 == '\0'` color check then descends left/right based on key comparison. The MS tree node is 0x24 bytes; US tree node is 0x30 bytes (extra 0x0C bytes for higher-resolution time storage). Both are std::map / std::set-style R-B trees keyed by absolute scheduled time.

**US-scheduler tick body FUN_00CF6080** (BCS-Y-1728 NEW, 856 bytes, sole caller [[LuaSchedulerTickUs_FUN_00CF63E0]] BCS-Y-1699): traverses the us-tree at scheduler+0x14, computes current-time-divided-by-1000 (us -> ms scale alignment), walks the tree via R-B color comparison to find ready entries (key <= now). For each ready entry, processes its child list (puVar3[7] field), invokes the dispatch via [[LuaScheduledDispatch_entry_FUN_00CF5EC0]] (BCS-Y-1686), frees consumed entries via FUN_0044D350. Also processes a separate vector at scheduler+0x30..+0x38 (auxiliary dispatch list?). The us-tree node has fields at: +0x0/+0x4/+0x8 = left/right/parent (R-B), +0x10/+0x14 = key (64-bit absolute time), +0x18 = ?, +0x1C = child list head, +0x20 = ?, +0x29 = color byte.

**TREE NODE ALLOCATORS (R-B tree sentinel constructors)**: [[LuaSchedulerUs_tree_node_alloc_FUN_00CF51A0]] (BCS-Y-1729 NEW, 59 bytes) allocates 0x30-byte us-tree head via FUN_0044D500 + initializes 3-pointer self-refs + color byte +0x29 = 1. [[LuaSchedulerMs_tree_node_alloc_FUN_00D0A870]] (BCS-Y-1730 NEW, 59 bytes) allocates 0x24-byte ms-tree head via FUN_0044D500 + similar init with color byte +0x21 = 1. The ms-tree allocator has 5 distinct callers (not just scheduler ctor) - reused for other R-B tree initializations in the engine.

**FUN_00D082A0 Lua-callable time getter** (BCS-Y-1731 NEW, 264 bytes): exposed to Lua scripts via LGE bootstrap FUN_00CD8990's cclosure-registration block. Computes seconds-since-epoch using QueryPerformanceCounter (FUN_004CFA50) divided by frequency (DAT_00F909C8). Has 2 code paths: one for high-precision (us-based), one for relative-to-epoch. Returns a double value. Likely registered as `_lge_getTime` or `_lge_clock` Lua API.

**MS-scheduler enqueue API call chain**: high-level callers identified but not deeply decomped: FUN_00CEF0F0's sole caller is FUN_00CE27F0; FUN_00CEF900's sole caller is FUN_00CEFA70. These are likely the closest-to-user-facing wrappers. Going further upstream would identify the actual Lua-callable `schedule(callback, ms_delay)` API entry. Deferred to follow-up.
